articles.title: US Dollar: Fragile strength hinges on Fed – Commerzbank

articles.title: USD/JPY: Yen carry risks build into Q4 – Rabobank
articles.expand: Rabobank’s Global Daily notes that FX markets were surprised by Dollar strength in Q3, with EUR/USD and GBP/USD relatively subdued while USD/JPY saw “huge action” higher. The report warns this move may spill over into the Yen Carry Trade if it continues. Emerging Market FX is also slipping against the Dollar again, except for CNY, which is treated as a separate case.

articles.title: Markets in upbeat mood, as UK economy surprises on the upside
articles.expand: Markets are in an upbeat mood this morning, and stocks and bonds are rallying together even though inflation in France was stronger than expected and UK GDP also received a surprise upside revision for the second quarter.

articles.title: TRY: Inflation and easing threaten Lira – Commerzbank
articles.expand: Commerzbank’s Tatha Ghose notes USD/TRY has broken above 49.0, continuing a pattern of defended levels being breached in step-jumps. He downplays the broader systemic impact of a Turkish stock market scandal and instead highlights surging fuel-driven inflation and the prospect of CBT rate cuts. Ghose warns that an easing cycle in an inflation-vulnerable economy is the key risk for the Lira.

articles.title: Australian Dollar: RBA tailwind seen fading – Commerzbank
articles.expand: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur argues that market expectations for 1.5 further Reserve Bank of Australia hikes look excessive after softer August CPI data. While inflation remains above target, he highlights lagged effects of past tightening and weakness in the real estate sector. Baur concludes the RBA is likely to wait, leaving the Australian Dollar unlikely to gain additional support.

articles.title: US Inflation: PCE revision seen as data clean-up – BNY
articles.expand: BNY Mellon’s Americas Macro Strategist John Velis argues that the upcoming PCE revision is a technical adjustment that will not alter the broader US inflation narrative. He highlights that portfolio management fees, which scaled with rising assets under management, distorted recent PCE readings versus CPI. The Bureau of Economic Analysis will shift to a labor-based methodology, improving the Fed’s preferred gauge without signaling real disinflation.

articles.title: Per Jansson in London on the economic situation
articles.expand: Last week, the Executive Board left the policy rate unchanged at 1.75 per cent and signalled that if the outlook for inflation and economic activity remains unchanged, it is expected that increases to the rate will begin this year. In London, Deputy Governor Per Jansson spoke at Nordea and the Swedish Chamber of Commerce for the United Kingdom about the economic situation and his reasoning behind the decision.
